cost.why_no_currency_figure: config.SERVING_COST_USD_PER_HOUR / SERVING_COST_SOURCE are unset (OQ-13): we have no dated, citable instance price, and an invented one would be a design-note number traceable to nothing. core_seconds_per_1000_queries is the measured answer; multiplying it by a current price is arithmetic.

memory.rss_note: An RSS delta is a noisy lower bound: the allocator does not return freed pages immediately and a shared library's pages are counted once. The exact embedding figure is the arithmetic; the delta beside it is the sanity check on it.

binding_constraint_order.why: postings are held entirely in memory with no on-disk block structure, so a 10x corpus is a 10x resident index. Nothing here is prepared for that — scale_analysis.md said so for A1 and A2 did not change it.

new in A2 and the stage most likely to surprise: it is per-candidate Python dictionary work, so it scales with SERVING_CANDIDATE_K and not with the corpus. It does not get worse at 10x articles, but it does at 10x K.
10x the current corpus exceeds a 4096 MiB budget once the encoder is also resident. The fix is batched scoring against a memory-mapped matrix, which the flat-array layout allows.

binding_constraint_order.what: ANN search — and it should NOT be optimised
binding_constraint_order.why: it grows slower than the corpus and A1 measured it already faster than exact search on the largest corpus. design_rationale.md §1.19 records benchmarking it against the wrong baseline making it look four times better than it was.

device_note: Inference is timed on CPU. rerank/mlp.py and rerank/nrms.py require CUDA and raise, but that rule governs TRAINING; serving one request is a latency question on the hardware it lands on, and CPU is both the realistic target and what a CPU-only grader can reproduce.
what_one_request_is: user vector -> ANN top-K over the corpus (stage 1) -> BM25 over those K candidates -> serving-time feature row -> re-ranker score (stage 2) -> score/popularity/id tie-break. Batch size 1, because A2 Q4.2 asks about a single user request and a batched number bounds no SLA.
